title: No More Stale Feedback: Co-Evolving Critics for Open-World Agent Learning
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a machine learning problem in critique-guided reinforcement learning for large language model agents: critics that provide natural-language feedback often become "stale" as the policy improves during on-policy training. The authors argue that static or frozen critics fail to adapt to shifting failure patterns, reducing the usefulness of feedback over time and limiting sample efficiency and long-horizon task performance.

To address this, the paper introduces ECHO (Evolving Critic for Hindsight-Guided Optimization), a framework in which the policy model and critic model are updated together in a synchronized co-evolutionary loop. The critic generates multiple score-aware diagnoses of an initial trajectory, the policy uses these critiques to produce refined trajectories, and both models are updated using group-relative policy optimization. The method also includes a saturation-aware reward shaping mechanism intended to value small but important improvements near the performance ceiling.

The study is not an education study and does not involve human learners, teachers, or K-12 instructional contexts. Instead, it evaluates LLM agents in open-world benchmark environments including WebShop, ALFWorld, SciWorld, and DeepSearch, using Qwen backbone models and comparisons against GRPO and several proprietary and open-source language models.

The main conclusion is that synchronized critic-policy co-evolution improves training stability and benchmark performance relative to standard GRPO and frozen-critic variants. The authors also conclude that failure patterns drift over training, making adaptive critics important, and that saturation-aware reward shaping helps especially with near-ceiling "last-mile" refinements. However, the framework depends heavily on the quality and calibration of the external reward model used to score trajectories and induced improvements.
quality_tier_rationale: This is not a K-12 education study and does not evaluate an educational intervention, learners, classrooms, or writing instruction. It is a technical AI methods paper on reinforcement learning for LLM agents in open-world benchmark environments.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports improvements on agent benchmark task success, not student learning, writing, revision, feedback, or K-12 instructional outcomes. Therefore it provides no direct evidence relevant to educational impact claims about generative AI for K-12 writing.
